rationale: Correct observation that "" is deliberately allowed (CommandResponseFromPlainText produces an empty ResponseType), but the cluster clears it and asserts no defect.

maxLength := 65535 is a function-local literal while the identical value already exists as PostMessageMaxBytesV2 in the same package (server/public/model/post.go:72); correct and actionable, but small.
A considered-and-cleared note asserting no defect; the clearing is also right, since the only call site (line 72) holds a non-nil value.

Same defect as the maintainer's "let's not throw a hard error, this might break existing servers" comment on that exact return: validation is welded into the decoder so callers cannot parse and then decide, and the fix (move it out of FromJSON) is what the thread asks for.

len(o.Text) counts bytes against a 65535 cap — the same byte-vs-rune defect the thread raises — and the cluster additionally grounds it in PostMessageMaxRunesV2/determineMaxPostSize (server/public/model/post.go:72-73), which is verified.

IsValid genuinely checks only ResponseType and Text, leaving IconURL/GotoLocation/ChannelId/Type/Props/Attachments unchecked; overlaps thread 4's demand that the URL fields be properly validated, though the thread targets laxness of a later-added check rather than its absence.
Verified: the only length case uses 65536 and expects an error; nothing pins that 65535 is accepted, so a > to >= change would pass the suite. Correct but small.

Accurate asymmetry — the stringify loop is one level deep while IsValid (lines 90-98) recurses without limit; actionable but low impact because nothing downstream consumes ExtraResponses beyond depth 1.

Verified contrast: HandleCommandResponse logs and continues per failing extra response, whereas the new recursive IsValid rejects the entire payload for one bad nested entry. Adjacent to thread 3's hard-error concern but makes a distinct, code-grounded claim about the recursion.

A null element in extra_responses survives the validator's nil-skip (command_response.go:91-93) and reaches HandleCommandResponsePost, where post.Type = response.Type dereferences it; the path from commandWebhook is unguarded, so this is a reachable panic the new strict validator could have closed.

Correct: the read error is discarded and (nil, nil) returned; DoCommandRequest compensates with an explicit nil check (server/channels/app/command.go:598) while commandWebhook does not. Pre-existing but a real silent failure adjacent to the change.

Verified: every non-error case in the table leaves response_type empty, and the two in_channel cases both expect errors, so the accept path of the new allowlist is untested in a PR whose stated purpose is validation plus tests.
A considered-and-cleared note that asserts no defect; it also reaches the opposite conclusion from thread 4, which wants the URL fields validated more strictly, so it is not a match.
Cleared note asserting no defect; the clearing is correct (server/public/go.mod declares go 1.26.3, so loop variables are per-iteration, and nothing escapes the loop).

No cap on len(ExtraResponses) anywhere, and each entry becomes a post insert plus broadcast; the global 300KB payload cap (server/channels/web/handlers.go:213-216) bounds but does not eliminate the amplification. Pre-existing, and the strict-validation change is the natural place to bound it.
Cleared note asserting no defect; the reading is right — the ShouldError branch previously asserted only assert.Nil(t, response).

Verified: Client4.ExecuteCommand/ExecuteCommandWithTeam decode server-emitted responses through the same CommandResponseFromJSON, so the new hard failure breaks existing Go clients — a concrete instance of the maintainer's "this might break existing servers, don't hard error here" objection, with the same remedy (validate at the ingest sites).
Considered-and-cleared note that asserts no defect introduced by the change.
True that the comment restates the condition, but this is purely stylistic and not worth a reviewer's attention.
Explicitly asserts no defect about an inert test literal.
Cleared note asserting no defect; correct, since the module targets go 1.26.3 where the range variable is per-iteration.
Cleared note asserting no defect; the clearing checks out — c.Err.WipeDetailed() runs whenever EnableDeveloper is off, and the two new detail strings are static.

Verified ordering: commandWebhook returns 400 on a parse/validation failure before HandleCommandWebhook reaches CommandWebhook().TryUse (server/channels/app/webhook.go:982), so the newly enlarged class of rejected bodies never consumes one of the five uses. Real but low impact.

The route is registered with APIHandlerTrustRequester (server/channels/web/webhook.go:21), whose handler wraps r.Body in http.MaxBytesReader with MaximumPayloadSizeBytes, so the body is bounded; the implied unbounded-read risk is wrong.
